title: Inspiration of Scripture
definition: The inspiration of Scripture is the truth that God breathed out His Word through human authors so that Scripture is truly His Word.
summary: Scripture is inspired by God and therefore trustworthy, authoritative, and profitable for His people.
christFocus: Jesus affirmed the reliability and authority of Scripture, and the inspired Word bears witness to His person, His saving work, His resurrection, and His return.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The doctrine of inspiration teaches that Scripture comes from God. Human authors truly wrote the books of the Bible, using their own language, settings, personalities, and circumstances, yet the Holy Spirit carried them along so that what was written is the Word God intended His people to receive.

Inspiration does not mean Scripture is merely inspiring or emotionally meaningful. It means Scripture has a divine source. The Bible speaks with authority because God speaks through it.

Because Scripture is inspired, it is profitable for teaching, reproof, correction, and training in righteousness. It reveals the truth of God, exposes the need of humanity, points to Christ, and equips believers for faithful life and ministry.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: If Scripture were only human reflection, believers would have no final certainty that its message is true. Inspiration matters because it grounds confidence in the Bible's authority and trustworthiness.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Approach Scripture with reverence and confidence. Read it as the Word God has given, not as a book to be reshaped by personal preference. Ask the Holy Spirit to help you understand and obey what He inspired.
